questions.stem: Newton's First Law states that an object will remain at rest or continue moving at constant velocity unless:

options.text: A resultant force acts on it

questions.explanation: Newton's First Law states that an object stays at rest or moves at constant velocity unless acted upon by a resultant (unbalanced) force.

questions.stem: What is the resultant force on an object moving at constant velocity?
questions.explanation: According to Newton's First Law, if an object moves at constant velocity, the forces are balanced and the resultant force is zero.

options.text: The tendency of an object to resist changes in its motion
The force needed to stop an object
The speed at which an object travels

questions.explanation: Inertia is the tendency of an object to resist changes in its motion. Objects with greater mass have greater inertia.

questions.stem: A book sits on a table without moving. The forces acting on it are:

options.text: Zero -- no forces act on a stationary object
Unbalanced, with the normal force being greater
Balanced, with weight equal to the normal reaction force

questions.explanation: The book is stationary, so by Newton's First Law the forces must be balanced. The downward weight equals the upward normal reaction force from the table.

questions.stem: A spacecraft in deep space has its engines turned off. According to Newton's First Law, it will:

options.text: Speed up because there is no friction

questions.explanation: With no resultant force acting on it (no friction or air resistance in space), the spacecraft continues at constant velocity indefinitely, as Newton's First Law predicts.

questions.stem: When the forces on an object are unbalanced, the object will:

options.text: Accelerate in the direction of the resultant force

questions.explanation: An unbalanced (resultant) force causes the object to accelerate in the direction of that resultant force.

questions.stem: Which object has the greater inertia?
questions.explanation: Inertia depends on mass. The bowling ball has the greatest mass of these objects and therefore the greatest inertia -- it is the hardest to start or stop moving.
